platform: native Windows x64, actual System32 bsdtar3.8.9 and Git for Windows GNU tar1.35, Node24; owned temporary filesystem only
problem: Windows bsdtar cannot convert original UTF-8 NUL-list names including 雪-💾 and corrupts/rejects some Unicode reads. Locale flags do not repair it; direct Unicode argv or dot-root can crash. These are real local tool failures, not a fixture encoding adjustment.
productionChanges: Only on Windows, resolve a real absolute GNU tar.exe from operator PATH or adjacent/standard Git for Windows installations, confirm --version, cache successful resolution keyed by PATH and installation-root environment.

Both local create and extraction use that absolute executable with shell:false and --force-local. No fallback to known-broken Windows bsdtar is used; absence produces actionable windows_workspace_archive_requires_gnu_tar.
Use winsymlinks:nativestrict for MSYS tar so extraction restores native symlinks or fails, never Cygwin text placeholders.

Preserve original streaming top-level NUL list, --exclude semantics, 32MiB child diagnostic buffer, namespaced long cwd and absence of dot-root entry; the POSIX tar command and arguments are unchanged.
Existing extractTarballToDirectory is now a named module export for direct real filesystem regression coverage; no REST/API contract changes.

scope: Real source directory beyond 260 characters; ASCII baseline retains exact bytes and no self entry.
Original Unicode and leading-dash member names, UTF-8 raw tar headers and binary bytes, nested exclusion/.git/resource-fork exclusion and no ./ self entry.
Real production extraction returns original bytes and actual native Unicode-target symlink.
Explicit followSymlinks dereferences source link; real extraction returns regular/hardlinked content with exact original bytes.
With PATH and Git roots isolated away from GNU tar, actual System32 bsdtar is rejected, no archive is created and original source bytes stay unchanged.

redRegression.method: Vitest transform only switches execTar back to original PATH tar and removes GNU --force-local injection; working-tree source is unchanged. Targeted original Unicode regression genuinely fails at bsdtar wchar_t conversion. Three pending results are name-filtered tests, not platform support skips.
redRegression.command: cd packages/adapter-utils; node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config ../../test-results/project-closure-20261029/tar-unicode-before.vitest.mjs src/tar-long-path.test.ts -t "preserves UTF-8 NUL entry names" --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile=../../test-results/project-closure-20261029/tar-unicode-before-red.json

experiments.scope: Original actual System32 tool: four LANG/LC_ALL variants, hdrcharset option, original direct Unicode argv and dot root all fail/crash.
Actual GNUtar --force-local preserves Unicode NUL name and bytes. 326-character cwd requires the existing Node namespace prefix; shorter cwd works both ways.
Independent System32 reader can list one Unicode member but Unicode argv extraction is corrupted/rejected, so actual production extraction plus raw archive bytes are the regression oracle.

intermediate.scope: Second test attempt 2/4: old ASCII and missing-tool tests passed; two failures exposed that System32 reader is also not a valid Unicode extraction oracle. Replaced those reader operations with raw header/body inspection and production extraction, preserving exact expected names and bytes.

limits: The 40,000-file / >32MiB manifest full-lane streaming test and adapter-utils whole-package final8 are run and reported separately by the root agent; this narrow receipt does not claim those passed.
Actual Windows native symlink extraction requires the Windows host to allow native symlink creation; strict mode fails rather than producing non-native placeholder files.
GNUtar/Git for Windows is now an explicit Windows local archive prerequisite. No dependency installation, lockfile modification, host Git configuration or external provider operation occurred.
New missing-GNU test is Windows-specific and runs on this host; all four applicable local tests passed with zero pending.
